papers.text: Grant the prize pumpkin the freedom of the town. It has asked very politely.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bus ticket museum in the old ticket office. Its own tickets go on show.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Set-up of may-ticket-museum. Other: the old ticket office is on the high street; the Guild wanted its window.

papers.text: Name the 7:02 bus after you, Mayor. It is late too, and also waves.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The clock tower's faces disagree. An inquiry will hear each face.
papers.subject: clocks
papers.biggerStudy: Both faces have spoken. The inquiry now wishes to hear the hands.
papers.note: Other: the face over the high street is the one the Guild opens by.

papers.text: Sign every bus ticket yourself, Mayor, so each journey is approved.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay for a sign on the bakery: 7:02 EXPECTED SHORTLY.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the sign goes on a shop wall.

papers.text: Keep the pothole by the shoe shop. It is all that slows the 7:02.
papers.subject: potholes
papers.note: Other: the Guild wants it filled; the spotters gather at it, by the glass.

papers.text: A hat, with compliments. It goes with anything, especially hats.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it wants a window seat on the 7:02. It has no ticket.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT GIVEN WINDOW SEAT ON THE 7:02

papers.text: The bean rows hide a third of the 7:02. Move one row, please.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Give the bus station a new lease of life. Mervyn has drafted one.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the works close the pavement by the shops.

papers.text: Be photographed boarding the 7:02, Mayor. Twice, in case of blur.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the 7:02 runs past the allotments; the growers wanted you that morning.

papers.text: A working group on why bus tickets are so small. It will report on one.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The report no longer fits. The group asks for a season pass.

papers.text: Unveil the new bus timetable, Mayor. Point at a likely time.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the timetable board stands in front of a shop window.

papers.text: Move the prize pumpkin out of Till's Teas. People ask its price.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The spotters keep an eye on our window. Move the stop: we want it back.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay to paint PROUDLY ADEQUATE on the bus station. Adequately.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Callback: the motto of the loading card.

papers.text: We would hire the bus station wall for a display. Then the bus.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Open the Guild's new window, Mayor. It does not open. Stand by it.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Sign to say our windows are windows, Mayor. We will frame it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A committee to word the OPEN sign. Two members favour AJAR.
papers.subject: signage
papers.biggerStudy: OPEN is agreed. The committee asks to begin on CLOSED.

papers.text: A committee to issue nose permits for shop windows. One nose each.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The nose committee asks to cover elbows too. And the odd forehead.

papers.text: A shop sign. Then a sign for the sign. Then a lamp for that one.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the sign hangs over the bus timetable.

papers.text: Mop the high street for the camera, Mayor. Just by the draper's.
papers.subject: ceremonies
papers.note: Other: the growers' barrows leave the soil there; they would rather it stayed theirs to sweep.

papers.text: A glass roof over the high street. Then glass sides. Then it is a window.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the growers want the rain that falls there.

papers.text: A sign at both ends of the high street: THE MAYOR'S HIGH STREET.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Swap the clock tower's face for yours, Mayor. Right twice a day.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Three visitors in four come for the pumpkin. The fourth is lost. Signs?
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the signs go up in the bus station.

papers.text: Cut the ribbon on our new compost bins, Mayor. Stand upwind.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the bins go behind the bus stop.

papers.text: Rodney promised our fence to the spotters. And to us, first.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Turn the clock tower to the allotments. Pumpkins it can see do 30 % better.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The 7:02 is not to hoot past the allotments. Nor the 7:15. Nor the clock.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for a parade permit. The parade is the pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will pay to rename the bus stop PUMPKIN CORNER. It is not a corner.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We would hire the bus station's parcel scales. Ours are too kind.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Pose with the prize pumpkin, Mayor. It prefers its left side.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Study the pothole on the high street. Its soil may be better than ours.
papers.subject: potholes
papers.biggerStudy: The soil is promising. The study now asks for a second pothole.

papers.text: A census of the prize pumpkin's admirers. So far: 312, some twice.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The census is complete. It now asks to count those who looked away.

papers.text: A committee on where the 7:02 should look as it passes our plots.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: Settled: it looks ahead. The committee now turns to the 7:15.

papers.text: Survey the vegetables' feelings about you, Mayor. Early signs are good.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A rain gauge for your desk. It is empty now, but one can hope.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the rain gauge: it wants the growers' best bed, for the view.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S RAIN GAUGE GIVEN PRIZE BED
clippings.refuse: RAIN GAUGE SENT BACK, STILL EMPTY
